label: Build stage
why: Tells us when your heating system will be needed, so your design is ready in time.

label: When do you need the goods on site?
hint: Your best guess is fine. Designs usually take 5–7 working days.

label: Who should we talk to about the design, if not you?
hint: Name, role and mobile, e.g. Dave, site manager, 07…
why: If a builder or architect is handling the detail, we'll go to them first and keep you copied.

label: what3words for the site (optional)
hint: ///word.word.word

label: We designed your quote from the plans you sent us. Are they still the current ones?
hint: Yes = nothing has changed since the quote. No = upload the newer revision below.
why: Plans change between quote and build. We design from the newest revision we hold, so a wall moved or a kitchen island added after the quote won't be on our drawings unless you send the new version. Not sure which revision we have? Say so in Anything else and we'll check with you.

label: New or extra plans
hint: PDF, DWG, photos or ZIP, up to 10 MB each.

label: I have files bigger than 10 MB
hint: Don't worry: tick this and your Project Engineer will send you a secure file request so you can send them directly.

label: Ceiling heights
hint: If your plans include sections, say so. Otherwise: assume 2.4 m, and list any rooms that differ, e.g. kitchen-diner vaulted to 4.2 m.
why: A good set of plans includes sections showing ceiling heights. Without them we need the height of every room and any vaulted areas, because the room volume sets its heat requirement.

label: Windows and external doors
hint: If your plans include elevations, say so. Otherwise: standard windows are about 1.2 m tall; tell us about bifolds, picture windows or lots of glazing.
why: Elevations show windows and doors to scale. With only floor plans we have the widths but not the heights, and glazing is where most heat is lost.

label: Kitchen, utility and bathroom layouts (optional)
why: We keep pipe out from under fitted units, islands, baths, showers and staircases. A kitchen or bathroom drawing, even a sketch, stops us heating under your island.

label: Anywhere we shouldn't heat?
hint: e.g. under the kitchen island and the bath. Garage and plant room unheated. Open staircase.
why: Fixed units, islands, baths and stairs are left unheated; tell us which rooms are out altogether.

label: Pick whichever is easiest
options: Upload the SAP calculation|Use my EPC|Describe it|New build: use the standard minimums
why: Your design service includes a heat loss calculation for every room, which sizes the heat pump and the pipe. For that we need a U-value for the walls, windows, roof and floor. A SAP calculation or an EPC already contains them; otherwise a rough description is enough, and for a new build we can use the Building Regulations minimums (walls 0.3, windows 1.8, roof 0.18, 70 mm floor insulation).

label: SAP calculation or EPC
hint: The full SAP calculation, not just the summary page.

label: Age of the property, or year built
hint: A mix of ages (an extension on an old house)? Say which rooms are which.

label: Walls
hint: Construction and insulation thickness.

label: Windows
hint: Double or triple glazed, frame type.

label: Roof
hint: Insulation thickness.

label: Floors
hint: Concrete, timber or beam and block; insulation thickness.

label: Walls
hint: Age, thickness, brick/stone/timber/cob, cavity filled?
why: For an existing house we work out each U-value from what the element is made of and how old it is.

label: Windows
hint: Age, single/double/triple glazed, wood/metal/uPVC.

label: Roof
hint: Age and insulation thickness.

label: Floors
hint: Age, concrete/timber/beam and block, insulation if any.

label: Where would you like the manifold(s)?
hint: e.g. utility room cupboard, and the airing cupboard upstairs. Or: marked on the plans.
why: Each manifold feeds the pipe loops around it, so its position sets how the loops are laid out and how far the pipe runs. A cupboard near the middle of the floor it serves is ideal.

label: Your boiler: type and where it is
hint: Combi, system or regular boiler, and the room it's in.
why: The boiler type decides how we connect the underfloor heating and whether a cylinder is involved.

label: Your heat pump: make, model and where it will go
why: We design the underfloor heating to suit the heat pump's flow temperature, so we need to know which one it is.

label: Your heat source and where it is
Hot water cylinder, if there is one
hint: e.g. airing cupboard upstairs. Or: none, combi boiler.

label: Screed floors: liquid or hand-mixed, and the depth
hint: Also say which floors or rooms are screed.
why: Liquid screed flows round the pipe and can be thinner; hand-mixed needs more depth over the pipe. The depth sets how quickly the floor warms up.

label: Joisted floors: joist type, direction and spacing, and any steels
hint: Say which floors or rooms. Joist type: Posi, TJI/I-joist, Eco or traditional timber. If the joist layout is on your plans, just say so. Steels: where they are and whether there's a 25 mm gap above or below them.
why: We draw the pipe between the joists, so we need their direction and spacing in each room. Engineered joists (Eco, TJI, Posi) let the pipe cross anywhere. Traditional timber joists have to be notched or battened, which limits where it can cross. Steels need a 25 mm gap for the pipe to pass, or they must be drilled, which your structural engineer has to agree.

label: Joist layout drawing (if you have one)
Over-floor areas (LoPro®): what is the subfloor, and how level is it?
hint: Say which floors or rooms. Concrete or timber; e.g. new slab, level. Or: old floor, falls about 20 mm across the room.
why: LoPro®Max goes on top of a structural subfloor and doesn't need to be perfectly level, because the self-levelling compound over the pipe corrects up to 30 mm in one pour. LoPro®10 needs a flat, level subfloor, which may need repairing first.

label: Acoustic floors: describe the floor build-up
hint: Say which floors or rooms.
why: Acoustic floors have extra layers; we need the build-up to place the pipe correctly.

label: Which floor construction are you having?
hint: We'll confirm this with you.
options: In floor, solid (screed)|In floor, joisted|Over-floor (LoPro®)|Acoustic|Not sure

label: Floor coverings, room by room
hint: e.g. tiles in kitchen and bathrooms, engineered wood in living room, carpet in bedrooms.
why: Carpet and thick wood slow the heat getting through, so the pipe spacing and flow temperature change with the covering.

label: Can pipes run through internal walls if needed?
why: Sometimes the shortest route to a room is through a wall rather than round it.

label: Where will the heat pump go?
hint: e.g. north gable wall by the utility room, 2.5 m from the fence. Or: marked on my plans.
why: An air source heat pump must be more than 1 m from the boundary to count as permitted development (3 m in Wales). Closer than that needs a planning application. It also needs clear airflow around it.

label: Cylinder, buffer tank and expansion vessels: where will they go?
hint: e.g. plant room off the utility, 1.2 m × 2 m, 2.4 m high.
why: We check your quoted cylinder and buffer actually fit the space (a cylinder up to 300 l can sit on a square 100 l buffer). There can be up to three expansion vessels.

label: Hot water cylinder location
hint: If different from the above.

label: Bedrooms
hint: We size hot water for bedrooms + 1 people unless you tell us otherwise.

label: How many hard surfaces are within 1 m of the heat pump? The ground always counts as one.
options: Two: the ground and the wall it's fixed to|Three: in a corner, or wall plus fence|Four or more: an alcove or enclosure
why: The MCS 020 noise assessment counts hard surfaces within 1 m that reflect sound. More than three fails the assessment.

label: What is next to the heat pump?
options: Open wall only|Wall and a fence|Corner of two walls|Alcove or enclosure

label: Your nearest neighbour's window or door
options: None nearby, open land|In direct view of the unit|Round a corner, not in view
why: We work out the sound level at your nearest neighbour's window or door, the assessment position. Whether the unit is in direct view from there changes the result.

label: Roughly how far from the heat pump, in metres?
hint: To the middle of their nearest window or door. Pacing it out is fine.

label: Describe that spot
hint: e.g. the kitchen window of number 6, across the side passage.

label: Rooms heated by radiators from the heat pump, not underfloor heating
hint: So they go in the heat loss calculation.

label: Ground source only: ground collector area or borehole
hint: Your quote states the area and pipe length allowed for; tell us where it will go, or mark up a site plan.

label: Marked-up plans for the heat pump or ground collector (optional)

section_title: Anything else for your Project Engineer?
label: Anything else
hint: Anything unusual: a warmer design temperature in one room, zoning you'd like, access, or something you'd like changed on the quote.
